summary: A description of a TENEX subsystem called SMFS for working with UCSB's Simple-Minded File System. It lets TENEX users store, retrieve, delete and rename files at UCSB. Files can be protected, and a file stored from one TENEX system can be retrieved from another.

plainLanguage.summary: SMFS is a TENEX program for managing files stored in UCSB's file system. Its commands can transfer, locate, rename, delete and protect files, with some limits on which files can be archived.

subtitle: A TENEX interface to UCSB's remote file storage

tldr.problem: TENEX users needed a terminal-based way to store and manage files in UCSB's Simple-Minded File System.
tldr.mechanism: The SMFS subsystem provides commands to copy or move files, locate them, delete or rename them, and set read or write passwords.
tldr.outcome: Users at supported TENEX systems could manage files in UCSB storage, subject to the file and naming limits described in the RFC.

today: RFC 409 documents a TENEX subsystem for using UCSB's Simple-Minded File System. It describes the commands and limitations of that implementation.

sections.title: The SMFS Interface
sections.content:
SMFS is a TENEX subsystem that connects users to the Simple-Minded File System at UCSB-MOD75. The server manages online direct-access storage. From a terminal, users can transfer files to and from UCSB and manage files stored there.

The document is written for readers familiar with TENEX and says SMFS was installed at SRI-ARC.
sections.plainLanguage: SMFS lets a TENEX user work with files stored at UCSB. The RFC explains the commands for using it from a terminal.

sections.title: File and Naming Limits
sections.content:
SMFS cannot archive long files in the TENEX sense. It also cannot handle a directory name, file name or extension containing non-alphanumeric characters, or a combined name longer than 32 characters. The RFC attributes these restrictions to naming limits at UCSB.

Files stored at UCSB can have read and write passwords, and a file archived from one TENEX system can be retrieved from another.
sections.plainLanguage: Some TENEX files cannot be archived because of their length or names. Files that are stored can be protected, and another TENEX system can retrieve them.

sections.title: Transferring and Managing Files
sections.content:
The COPY command transfers a file while leaving the source unchanged. MOVE works like COPY but deletes the source after a successful transfer. LOCATE checks whether a file is archived at UCSB; DELETE removes a stored file; and RENAME changes its name.

Users can specify a host with a file name for transfers between TENEX systems. If a host is omitted, the local TENEX system is used as the default.
sections.plainLanguage: COPY keeps the source file, while MOVE removes it after a successful transfer. Other commands check whether a file is stored, delete it or change its name.

sections.title: User Details and File Passwords
sections.content:
SMFS keeps a user name and account for requests to the UCSB server. The defaults come from the user's TENEX login directory and the account value described in the RFC. Users can inspect or change those values with USER NAME and ACCOUNT commands.

Separate read and write passwords can protect files stored at UCSB. The PASSWORD command sets or clears the password values used by later commands.
sections.plainLanguage: SMFS uses a user name and account when it contacts UCSB. Users can set passwords that control reading or changing stored files.
